title: A parent’s AI playbook keeps core skills while making room for new tools
friendlyTitle: Children can learn AI without giving up reading, writing and thinking
summary: Economist and father Daniel Susskind argues that children should learn to use AI without outsourcing the foundational skills needed to judge its work. He describes creative family uses alongside concerns about synthetic media, education and whether children understand what an assistant produces for them.
friendlySummary: Daniel Susskind says children need experience with AI because it will be part of their world. They also need strong basic skills so they can understand and question its answers.
whyItMatters: The useful middle ground is neither unrestricted use nor pretending the tools will disappear. Parents and teachers can protect periods of unaided reading, writing and problem-solving, then use AI for critique, exploration and creation where the child remains an active participant.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Families and schools can set times for work without AI, then use it for feedback and creative experiments. The child should still think, choose and explain.
